external_entities.name: Duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

external_entities.name: Scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: Dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript app used by duty engineers to call the dispatch API and receive live job status.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

processes.name: Corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: Dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer; it reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: Schedule importer
processes.description: A scheduled process that pulls and parses the partner's SOAP feed, archives downloaded documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token when posting to the dispatch API. The token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

data_stores.name: Dispatch database
data_stores.description: The database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: Every job order in it carries the token or the session that created it, and nothing about the person behind that token. How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: Schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder on the corporate file store containing each document downloaded by the schedule importer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_stores.name: Corporate file store
data_stores.description: The corporate file store on which the schedule archive folder resides.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store
data_stores.notes: The text does not state the network zone of the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: load console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer loads the dispatch console from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser. The console is a single-page JavaScript app and our corporate web host serves it.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and the API are served from different origins. The API answers the console cross-origin. The permitted origins and credential behavior were not recorded.

data_flows.name: stream live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether that socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

data_flows.name: read and write dispatch records
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: Job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.

data_flows.name: pull planned work
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS every hour.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS and parses the XML document it gets back.
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies our importer, or how our importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: Tomorrow's planned work in an XML document.

data_flows.name: write schedule archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded partner document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_flows.data_description: Downloaded XML documents containing planned work.

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls. It presents an API token.
data_flows.notes: The API token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: Production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate, with authority to move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of the control-plane rights. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: Scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the scheduling partner, which is another company.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company
